rationale: The hypothesis asserts that biallelic NOTCH3 cases typically begin in the 3rd to 5th decades of life with subcortical lacunar strokes and progressive cognitive impairment. This is partially supported for biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants, which cause an early-adulthood CADASIL-spectrum phenotype. However, it is explicitly contradicted for biallelic loss-of-function/null NOTCH3 variants (the classical cause of autosomal recessive NOTCH3-related leukoencephalopathy/leukodystrophy), which manifest in infancy or early childhood (congenital to 9–14 months) with global developmental delay, seizures, spasticity, and childhood-onset strokes rather than adult-onset symptoms.

evidence.text: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in NOTCH3 (26 patients) cause a neurodevelopmental disorder with spasticity, childhood-onset stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss, whereas biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients) manifest with early adulthood-onset stroke and dementia within the CADASIL spectrum.

source.title: Clinical and neuroradiological spectrum of biallelic variants in NOTCH3
source.quote: Biallelic loss-of-function variants (26 patients) lead to a neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by spasticity, childhood-onset stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia. Conversely, patients with biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients) fall within CADASIL spectrum phenotype with early adulthood onset stroke, dementia, and deep white matter lesions without significant volume loss.

evidence.text: A compound heterozygous patient carrying a CADASIL cysteine-altering variant (p.Cys1146Ser) and a frameshift loss-of-function variant (p.Cys1024Valfs248) in trans developed progressive gait disturbance, slurred speech, and dysphagia beginning in his mid-thirties, with multiple lacunes and extensive white matter lesions.

source.title: An in trans NOTCH3 loss-of-function variant modifies disease severity in CADASIL: A family-based study
source.quote: The proband, carrying p.Cys1146Ser and p.Cys1024Valfs248 in trans, developed progressive gait disturbance, dysphagia, and slurred speech beginning in his mid-thirties. Brain MRI demonstrated extensive white matter hyperintensities, multiple lacunar infarcts, and numerous cerebral microbleeds.

conflicts: Age of onset differs drastically by variant mechanism: biallelic loss-of-function (LoF) variants present in infancy (9–14 months) or childhood with developmental delay, seizures, and spasticity, whereas biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants present in early adulthood with strokes and dementia.

Neuroradiological patterns differ between variant categories: biallelic LoF variants show periatrial white matter volume loss and sparing of the anterior temporal pole, unlike CADASIL-associated cysteine variants.

new_directions.question_text: Does residual NOTCH3 signaling activity explain the phenotypic divide between biallelic missense versus biallelic truncating loss-of-function variants?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying why cysteine missense variants mimic aggressive dominant CADASIL while null/loss-of-function variants produce infantile/childhood-onset leukodystrophy will refine classification criteria for recessive NOTCH3-related disorders.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true prevalence and penetrance of livedo racemosa and anterior temporal lobe sparing in recessive NOTCH3 loss-of-function cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Anterior temporal lobe involvement is a hallmark of CADASIL, but multiple recessive NOTCH3 LoF reports highlight anterior temporal pole sparing and livedo racemosa, which could serve as key differential diagnostic biomarkers.
